extracted_factors.Label: Deforestation in Indonesia
extracted_factors.Description: Deforestation is a significant contributor to Indonesia's GHG emissions, mainly due to agricultural expansion, logging, and mining. It directly affects climate targets and the livelihoods of indigenous and rural communities.

extracted_factors.Label: REDD+ Program Design
extracted_factors.Description: The REDD+ program structure aims to mitigate deforestation through policy implementation and international cooperation. It indirectly drives forest conservation efforts by providing guidelines and frameworks for action.

extracted_factors.Label: International Climate Agreements
extracted_factors.Description: Agreements like the Paris Accord foster international cooperation and commitment, compelling nations like Indonesia to engage in initiatives such as REDD+ to meet global environmental goals.

extracted_factors.Label: Institutional Capacity
extracted_factors.Description: The capacity of Indonesia's institutions to implement REDD+ effectively influences the program's success. Institutional weaknesses can hinder the enforcement and benefits realization of REDD+.

extracted_factors.Label: Stakeholder Participation
extracted_factors.Description: The involvement of various stakeholders, including indigenous groups, affects the effectiveness and fairness of REDD+. Greater participation can lead to more equitable outcomes and better adherence to environmental justice.

extracted_factors.Label: Financial Compensation for Conservation
extracted_factors.Description: REDD+ offers financial incentives to preserve forests, directly driving forest owners and local communities to engage in conservation activities, thus reducing deforestation.

extracted_factors.Label: Program Criticism and Challenges
extracted_factors.Description: Critiques of REDD+ highlight challenges such as adequacy of financial incentives, stakeholder engagement, and compensation mechanisms. These impact the perceived and actual effectiveness of the program.
